quote: In the context of economic evaluations of health interventions, spillovers are all impacts from an intervention on all parties or entities other than the users of the intervention under evaluation.

“Spillover costs” refers to impacts on others in terms of resource uses valued in monetary terms, such as productivity costs.

quote: These reviews highlight that only a minority (4–23%) of the studies included the HRQoL of others, even in disease areas where the effects are expected to be substantial, such as Alzheimer’s disease or paediatric diseases.

value: Where others' health-related quality of life was included, cost-effectiveness ratios generally decreased.
quote: Although fewer than half of the studies (15 out of 40) reported the impact of including others’ HRQoL measurements on the calculation of incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICER), when they did, the ratios generally decreased (in 10 out of 15 studies).
